question: A technical writer generates two drafts of an API integration guide, one for experienced developers and one for low-code platform users, and needs to check them for consistency before publishing. What should the writer confirm?
options: A) Both drafts must describe the same steps and results, varying only in terminology and depth.
B) The writer should check that both drafts have identical code samples to ensure uniformity.
C) The low-code draft should omit authentication, as low-code users only need the base URL.
D) The developer draft should simply be essentially a condensed version of the low-code guide.
correct_answers: A) Both drafts must describe the same steps and results, varying only in terminology and depth.
explanations: Correct. Both drafts should describe the same underlying steps and outcomes, ensuring consistency across audiences. The only acceptable differences are in terminology and level of detail appropriate for each user group.

Incorrect. Requiring identical code samples overlooks the fact that experienced developers and low-code platform users interact with the API differently. Low-code users may not use code samples at all, or they might need platform-specific snippets that differ from the developer draft.

Incorrect. Low-code users still need authentication information to use the API securely. Omitting authentication entirely and providing only a base URL would leave them with incomplete setup instructions.

Incorrect. The developer draft should not be a condensed version of the low-code guide; each audience requires distinct structure and depth. Developers need in-depth technical details and code examples, while low-code users need simplified configuration steps.
